name: 2WayMicropay
author: DReardon

sections.description:
Sell Content. Reward Users.

Qixit’s 2WayMicropay plugin turns WordPress links, posts, pages, comments, images, videos, audio, downloads, and other digital content into purchase or payout opportunities.

Instead of relying only on advertising, subscriptions, or high-priced products, publishers can offer visitors an à-la-carte payment option priced in Qix Credits — including prices as low as one cent.

Unlike conventional payment and paywall systems, value can flow in both directions:

  • Visitors can pay to unlock content, play media, publish posts, or submit comments.
  • Publishers can give visitors free trial credits or reward them for viewing ads, following links, or completing other actions.
  • Publishers and creators can share revenue and referral commissions.

Qixit is the company and account platform. 2WayMicropay is Qixit’s two-way micropayment product.

Before You Use the Plugin

To activate 2WayMicropay on a WordPress website, the site owner must:

  1. Create a free Qixit account at qixit.com/create-an-account.
  2. Obtain Qixit Vendor Credentials at register.qixit.com/register.

Vendor credentialing currently costs $10.

Your Vendor Credentials allow you to:

  • Create purchase links
  • Create payout links
  • Create and manage products
  • Receive payments and credits
  • Access vendor tools and reports
  • Obtain the API code required to automate the creation and management of 2WayMicropay hyperlinks on your website.

What You Can Do

The plugin supports multiple ways to monetize and promote your WordPress site:

  • Premium posts and pages — Charge for articles, tutorials, reports, downloads, images, videos, audio, and other content.
  • Free preview with paid continuation — Show an introduction and charge visitors to continue reading.
  • Pay once, view forever — Let a buyer purchase permanent access to selected content.
  • Pay per view — Require a new payment for each access or use.
  • Time-limited access — Sell access that expires after a specified number of hours.
  • Session-only access — Allow access during the current visit or session.
  • Pay-per-play media — Charge users to play a video, song, podcast, game, speech, or other embedded experience.
  • Paid comments — Require a small payment before a visitor can submit a comment.
  • Paid author and contributor access — Charge users for author rights, contributor privileges, or publication of an article.
  • Creator revenue sharing — Allocate a percentage of eligible revenue to the author or content creator.
  • Referral commissions — Reward users and partners who refer purchasers or new users.
  • Payout links — Give credits to visitors for viewing an ad, following a link, completing a survey, or taking another desired action.
  • Free trial credits — Give users site credits they can spend on your own content.

Convert Existing Content Quickly

You do not need to edit every post or page one at a time.

2WayMicropay makes it easy to selectively update:

  • A single post or page
  • A chosen group of posts or pages
  • All selected content within a category or search result
  • Large groups of existing posts or pages through WordPress bulk actions

From the WordPress Posts or Pages screen, site owners can select multiple items and apply 2WayMicropay settings in one operation.

For example, you can:

  • Convert selected posts to permanent paid access
  • Convert selected posts to pay-per-view access
  • Return selected content to free access
  • Synchronize selected products with the Qixit API
  • Apply premium settings only to archived, high-value, or specialty content

This allows a publisher to begin with a small test group, expand gradually, or convert a large content archive without opening and editing each item individually.

Monetize More Than Content

2WayMicropay can create revenue from interactions that are normally free.

You can charge users to:

  • Download a report, file, image, or ebook
  • Watch a video or listen to audio
  • Play a game or access an interactive feature
  • Read the premium portion of an article
  • Obtain author or contributor privileges
  • Publish a post on your site
  • Submit a comment

Paid comments can also block automated spam and low-effort submissions. Site owners remain responsible for their own editorial, moderation, and refund policies.

Motivate Your Audience and Your Content Creators

Purchase links collect credits from users. Payout links move credits in the other direction.

Use payout links and promotional credits to:

  • Give visitors free trial credits
  • Pay users to view an advertisement
  • Reward completion of a survey or promotional action
  • Encourage visitors to visit a sponsor’s page
  • Reward referrals or participation
  • Introduce new users to paid content without requiring them to fund an account first

Payout links can include budgets, expiration dates, and other conditions.

In addition, you can automatically share a percentage of your revenue with contributing authors, content creators, and those who refer their followers to your content.

Built for Flexible Pricing

Different content calls for different pricing and access rules. The plugin lets you experiment with:

  • Free access
  • Pay once, view forever
  • Pay per view
  • Limited-hour access
  • Session-only access

Prices may range from very small micropay amounts, down to a single penny, up to several dollars in Qix Credits.

This makes it possible to monetize low-value, high-volume content that may be difficult to sell through conventional credit-card transactions.

Simple Purchase Flow

When a visitor selects premium content:

  1. The price is displayed.
  2. The visitor signs in or creates a free Qixit account.
  3. The visitor confirms the purchase.
  4. Access is delivered after successful payment.

The publisher does not need to build a separate checkout or subscription system.

Manage Products and Transactions

The plugin connects WordPress to the Qixit 2WayMicropay Products API.

Depending on the feature being used, publishers can:

  • Create and synchronize products from WordPress
  • Create purchase and payout links
  • Manage products through Qixit’s vendor tools
  • Review product and sales activity
  • Configure payout budgets and expiration dates
  • Map WordPress authors to Qixit accounts
  • Set default and post-specific revenue shares
  • Review transactions and account activity

Designed for Publishers and Creators

Qixit’s 2WayMicropay can be used by:

  • News and magazine publishers
  • Independent writers and bloggers
  • Musicians, podcasters, and video creators
  • Course and tutorial publishers
  • Game developers
  • Photographers and artists
  • Membership and community sites
  • Multi-author publications
  • Advertisers and sponsors
  • Sites that want to reward engagement

Whether you publish one premium download or operate a large content archive, the plugin gives you a flexible way to test prices and create new revenue streams.

Why Two-Way Micropayments?

Traditional payment systems move value primarily from the customer to the seller.

Qixit’s 2WayMicropay platform also allows publishers, advertisers, and sponsors to send credits to users.

Visitors may receive free promotional credits and then use those credits to sample premium content. This reduces the barrier to trying micropayments and helps publishers introduce paid content gradually.

The system is designed to support both spending and earning at true micropay rates. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

WordPress Demonstrates the Broader Platform

The WordPress plugin demonstrates how easily Qixit’s 2WayMicropay platform can be added to a website.

Custom websites and applications can also use the developer API to automate:

  • Product creation
  • Purchase links
  • Payout links
  • Access rules
  • Revenue sharing
  • Other payment and reward workflows

Important Information About Qix Credits

Qix Credits are platform credits and are not cash or legal tender.

Dollar-and-cent values may be used for display convenience. Redemption and withdrawal eligibility are governed by Qixit’s applicable agreements, policies, credentialing requirements, and account rules.

Use of the plugin and related services is subject to the Qixit and 2WayMicropay terms, privacy policies, software license, and service agreements.

Learn More

  • Create a free Qixit account
  • Obtain Qixit Vendor Credentials
  • Plugin instructions and setup guide
  • Benefits for content creators and publishers
  • 2WayMicropay demonstrations

External services

This plugin connects to Qixit-hosted services to create/sync products, verify purchases, and render purchase/payment flows.

Service endpoints used by this plugin may include:

  • Products API base URL configured in plugin settings (default Qixit endpoints)
  • https://products.qixit.com for frontend purchase/payment user flows
  • https://products.qixit.com/sdk/qixit.js for purchase/embed runtime behavior
  • Branding manifest endpoint (/api/branding/config) when branding assets are loaded

Data sent to Qixit services may include:

  • Site API key (X-API-Key) configured by the site owner
  • App identifier (X-App-ID) used for integration attribution (non-secret)
  • Product and payout identifiers (GUIDs)
  • Callback and delivery URLs for products
  • Transaction IDs for purchase verification (GET /api/Purchase/verify/{transactionId})
  • Qixit buyer username for ownership checks and paid-comment verification
  • Server-to-server ReportUrl callbacks authenticated with HMAC (X-Qixit-Signature) using the site API key

ReportUrl callbacks from Products Portal cannot use WordPress nonces; they are authenticated with HMAC signatures and verified against Products Portal before any purchase is recorded locally.

Browser return URLs from hosted Qixit checkout also cannot carry wp-admin nonces. Those callbacks use one-time qixit_cb transients (issued when checkout starts) plus server-side transaction verification against Products Portal before any local purchase, role change, or account action is applied.

Author account creation (optional paid service)

Author Commerce and paid author signup are disabled by default. A site owner must explicitly enable Author Commerce in plugin settings, configure fees and terms, and place the [qixit_become_an_author] shortcode (or equivalent onboarding flow) before any public account creation can occur.

When enabled, visitors can pay for author rights through Qixit checkout. After a verified payment callback, the plugin may call wp_insert_user() once to create the WordPress account requested in the signup form. This is not a generic public registration endpoint:

  • The feature is opt-in only (qixit_enable_author_commerce defaults to off).
  • Signup starts with a nonce-protected AJAX/form request and stores a short-lived signup transient until checkout completes.
  • Checkout requires a matching one-time callback token and a verified Products Portal transaction ID before any account is created or role is assigned.
  • Existing WordPress usernames are rejected; existing users must log in and purchase author rights while authenticated.
  • Role assignment (Contributor when moderation is enabled, otherwise Author) follows the site owner’s Author Commerce settings.
  • Site owners receive admin notices for signup events (including duplicate-email reconciliation) and can disable Author Commerce, change fees, or remove/block users at any time from wp-admin.
  • The plugin does not call wp_signon() or wp_set_auth_cookie(); WordPress core handles login after account creation.

A Qixit vendor account and site API key configured by the site owner are required.

The service is provided by 2WayMicropay/Qixit:

  • Terms: https://qixit.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://qixit.com/privacy
  • Learn more about 2WayMicropay: https://2waymicropay.com/
sections.installation:
Requirements Before Installation

To activate Qixit’s 2WayMicropay plugin on your WordPress website, you will need:

  • A WordPress website on which you can install plugins
  • A free Qixit account
  • Qixit Vendor Credentials
  • The API code provided with your Vendor Credentials

Vendor credentialing currently costs $10.

Step 1: Create Your Free Qixit Account

  1. Go to qixit.com/create-an-account.
  2. Create your free Qixit account.
  3. Complete the account setup and verification steps.
  4. Keep your Qixit sign-in information available for the vendor registration process.

A Qixit account is required because Qixit is the account and credit platform used by 2WayMicropay.

Step 2: Obtain Vendor Credentials

  1. Go to register.qixit.com/register.
  2. Complete the Qixit Vendor Credential registration.
  3. Pay the current $10 credentialing fee.
  4. Complete any required identity, business, or website information.
  5. Save the Vendor Credentials and API code provided for your website.

Your Vendor Credentials allow you to:

  • Create products
  • Create purchase links
  • Create payout links
  • Receive payments and credits
  • Access vendor reporting and management tools
  • Connect your WordPress site to the 2WayMicropay API

The API code provided through the vendor credentialing process is required to activate 2WayMicropay on your website.

Step 3: Install the Plugin from WordPress.org

  1. Sign in to your WordPress administrator dashboard.
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  3. Search for 2WayMicropay.
  4. Select the official Qixit 2WayMicropay plugin.
  5. Click Install Now.
  6. When installation is complete, click Activate.

Manual Installation

  1. Download the plugin ZIP file.
  2. Sign in to your WordPress administrator dashboard.
  3. Go to Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  4. Click Upload Plugin.
  5. Select the ZIP file.
  6. Click Install Now.
  7. Click Activate Plugin.

Experienced administrators may also extract the plugin folder into:

/wp-content/plugins/

Then activate it from the WordPress Plugins screen.

Step 4: Connect WordPress to Qixit

  1. Open 2WayMicropay > Settings.
  2. Enter the requested Qixit vendor information.
  3. Enter the API code or Site API Key supplied with your Vendor Credentials.
  4. Save the settings.
  5. Confirm that the connection status displays Connected.

The API connection allows WordPress to create and synchronize purchase products, payout products, access settings, and related transactions with Qixit’s 2WayMicropay platform.

If the connection does not succeed:

  1. Confirm that the Vendor Credentials are active.
  2. Confirm that the API code was copied correctly.
  3. Confirm that the code is assigned to the correct website.
  4. Save the settings again.
  5. Use the plugin’s diagnostic or connection-testing tools when available.

Step 5: Monetize One Post or Page

  1. Open an existing post or page, or create a new one.
  2. Find the 2WayMicropay Settings panel.
  3. Choose the access type:
  • Regular — Free
  • Pay Once, View Forever
  • Pay Per View
  • Limited Hours
  • Session Only
  1. Enter the price in Qix Credits.
  2. Optionally enable Use Read More as paywall.
  3. Publish or update the post.
  4. Confirm that the product synchronized successfully with the Qixit API.
  5. Test the purchase flow as a visitor.

Add a Free Preview

  1. Edit the premium post or page.
  2. Add a WordPress More block, or insert the <!--more--> tag, after the free introduction.
  3. Enable Use Read More as paywall in the 2WayMicropay Settings.
  4. Save or update the content.

Visitors can read the portion above the break for free. The remaining content is delivered after payment.

Convert Multiple Posts or Pages at Once

You do not need to edit every post or page individually.

To selectively convert a group of posts or pages:

  1. Go to Posts > All Posts or Pages > All Pages.
  2. Use WordPress filters, categories, search, dates, or authors to identify the desired content.
  3. Select the individual posts or pages you want to update.
  4. Open the Bulk Actions menu.
  5. Choose the appropriate 2WayMicropay action.
  6. Click Apply.
  7. Review the updated items and confirm synchronization with the API.

Available bulk actions may include:

  • Set Premium — Pay Once, View Forever
  • Set Premium — Pay Per View
  • Set as Free
  • Synchronize Selected Products to API

This makes it easy to:

  • Convert an archive of older articles to paid access
  • Monetize only selected categories
  • Test paid access on a small group of posts
  • Convert premium reports or specialty content
  • Return selected items to free access
  • Update large groups of posts or pages without opening each one

You may repeat the process for different groups and assign different access rules or prices.

Enable Paid Comments

  1. Edit the applicable post or page.
  2. Find the 2WayMicropay Settings panel.
  3. Enable Require payment for comments.
  4. Enter the comment price.
  5. Save or update the post.
  6. Test the comment payment and submission process.

For a site-wide default:

  1. Go to 2WayMicropay > Settings.
  2. Enable Global Paid Comments.
  3. Enter the default price.
  4. Save the settings.

Post-specific settings may override the global setting.

Configure Author Commerce

  1. Go to 2WayMicropay > Settings.
  2. Open Author Commerce Settings.
  3. Enable Author Commerce.
  4. Select whether paid applicants become Authors or Contributors.
  5. Set the Author Rights fee.
  6. Optionally set a per-publication fee.
  7. Set the default author revenue share.
  8. Optionally enable revenue sharing from paid comments.
  9. Enter the author terms and instruction-page URL.
  10. Save the settings.
  11. Publish the author-rights purchase page using the plugin shortcode.
  12. Confirm that participating authors have valid Qixit account identifiers mapped to their WordPress accounts.

Test the complete author signup, payment, approval, publishing, and revenue-sharing workflow before opening it to the public.

Create a Payout Link

  1. Sign in to the Qixit vendor or Products Portal.
  2. Create a payout product or payout link.
  3. Enter the payout amount.
  4. Choose whether the payout uses Qix Credits or site promotional credits.
  5. Enter the destination URL.
  6. Set the payout budget.
  7. Set an expiration date, when appropriate.
  8. Copy the generated payout URL or product identifier.
  9. Add the payout link or shortcode to the WordPress post or page.
  10. Preview and test the complete flow.

Payout links can be used to:

  • Give free trial credits
  • Pay visitors to view an ad
  • Reward a referral
  • Reward survey completion
  • Encourage visits to a sponsor page
  • Motivate another desired action

Configure Pay-Per-Play Media

  1. Sign in to the Qixit vendor or Products Portal.
  2. Create or edit the applicable product.
  3. Enter the price.
  4. Choose the appropriate pay-per-play or single-use access setting.
  5. Copy the Product GUID or product identifier.
  6. Add the plugin shortcode to the WordPress post or page.
  7. Enter the Product GUID in the shortcode.
  8. Add or embed the associated video, audio, game, or other media.
  9. Save and test the page.

Final Testing Checklist

Before promoting paid or rewarded content, verify that:

  • Your free Qixit account is active
  • Your Vendor Credentials are active
  • The $10 credentialing process has been completed
  • The correct API code is entered
  • The plugin reports Connected
  • Products synchronize successfully
  • Prices and access rules are correct
  • Bulk-updated posts or pages have the intended settings
  • The free preview ends in the correct location
  • The purchase frame opens correctly
  • New users can create a Qixit account
  • Existing users can sign in
  • Successful payments unlock the intended content
  • Payout links use the correct amount, budget, and expiration date
  • Author accounts and revenue shares are mapped correctly
  • The experience works on desktop and mobile devices

For detailed configuration examples and troubleshooting, visit the official plugin guide:

2waymicropay.com/wp/download-the-2waymicropay-wordpress-plugin
sections.faq:
Is the plugin required to use 2WayMicropay links on every website?

No. Purchase and payout links can be copied and pasted to any website or social media page. Anyone with a Vendor certification can manually create and manage these links. The plugin is only necessary to automate this process for WordPress sites.

Can I use the API to enable 2WayMicropay hyperlink management on other web sites?

Yes. To obtain access to the API, you will need Developer credentials that can be obtained at register.qixit.com/register. You can do anything, and more, that is done in this WordPress plugin on any website using our secure API and the credentials we will provide to you.

Can I allow unpaid comments?

Yes. In the post settings metabox, select either paid comments or unpaid comments.

Does this plugin ship privileged developer secrets?

No. The plugin does not embed a privileged developer API secret.
sections.changelog:
4.1.5

  • Fixes author signup checkout failing to open when browsers block popups opened after async AJAX (pre-opens checkout window on click).
  • Syncs paid-comment product price to Products Portal before display/checkout so tooltip and confirmation amounts match.
  • Opens paid-comment checkout in the on-page overlay for reliable confirmation without popup blockers.
  • Verifies paid comments by transaction ID (pay-per-play products are never marked “owned” in the API).
  • Forces author signup checkout to prompt for login and require a fresh payment (pay-per-checkout access mode).
  • Suppresses duplicate delivery-tab opens for paid comments and author signup in Edge; author signup uses iframe overlay instead of popups.
  • Relaxes author signup payment verification to trust the portal transaction ID and buyer username (fixes alias/amount mismatch after successful checkout).
  • Fixes publication-fee callbacks returning to the post editor, verifies payment by transaction ID, and permanently waives republish fees once a post is published.

Browser return URLs from hosted Qixit checkout also cannot carry wp-admin nonces. Those callbacks use one-time qixit_cb transients (issued when checkout starts) plus server-side transaction verification against Products Portal before any local purchase, role change, or account action is applied.

Author account creation (optional paid service)

Author Commerce and paid author signup are disabled by default. A site owner must explicitly enable Author Commerce in plugin settings, configure fees and terms, and place the [qixit_become_an_author] shortcode (or equivalent onboarding flow) before any public account creation can occur.

When enabled, visitors can pay for author rights through Qixit checkout. After a verified payment callback, the plugin may call wp_insert_user() once to create the WordPress account requested in the signup form. This is not a generic public registration endpoint:

  • The feature is opt-in only (qixit_enable_author_commerce defaults to off).
  • Signup starts with a nonce-protected AJAX/form request and stores a short-lived signup transient until checkout completes.
  • Checkout requires a matching one-time callback token and a verified Products Portal transaction ID before any account is created or role is assigned.
  • Existing WordPress usernames are rejected; existing users must log in and purchase author rights while authenticated.
  • Role assignment (Contributor when moderation is enabled, otherwise Author) follows the site owner’s Author Commerce settings.
  • Site owners receive admin notices for signup events (including duplicate-email reconciliation) and can disable Author Commerce, change fees, or remove/block users at any time from wp-admin.
  • The plugin does not call wp_signon() or wp_set_auth_cookie(); WordPress core handles login after account creation.

A Qixit vendor account and site API key configured by the site owner are required.
